source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

properties.source: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
properties.materialScope: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastics >0.33 mm, combined size classes
properties.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
properties.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.
properties.coverageMeaning: Fraction of tile water assigned a base-cell model estimate; not the fraction physically sampled.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

metadata.areaMethod: WGS84 ellipsoidal equal-area projected metres (EPSG:6933; polar caps EPSG:6931/6932)
metadata.aggregation: Latest-date mean per compatible 1 km² base cell, then clipped-water-area weighted mean of supported base cells; no missing-cell zero fill.
metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
metadata.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.

coastline.name: Natural Earth 1:10m land
coastline.limitations: Cartographic 1:10,000,000 coastline, not 10-metre spatial resolution. Small islands, tidal change and fine shorelines may be omitted; especially uncertain for 1 km² coastal cells. Natural Earth flags northern Russia and southern Chile coastline accuracy.

metadata.coastlineLimitations: Natural Earth 1:10 million cartographic land polygons; small islands, fine shorelines and tides may be missing. Coastal 1 km² cells are especially uncertain.
metadata.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

gradient.method: Gaussian-weighted visual interpolation within 75 km of a source point (25 km bandwidth). Not a validated pollution model or measured coverage.
gradient.waterMask: Natural Earth 1:10m with conservative raster edge buffer

colorScale.domainBasis: 0 to the 95th percentile of the selected source concentrations; colors saturate above this endpoint, displayed densities do not.
colorScale.note: Continuous concentration colors use a square-root scale; these are separate from the fixed SPI classification colors.

gradient.note: Continuous blue-to-red concentration scale. SPI classification remains available in tile details. Transparent beyond support or on land.
gradient.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

metadata.areaMethod: WGS84 ellipsoidal equal-area projected metres (EPSG:6933; polar caps EPSG:6931/6932)
metadata.aggregation: Latest-date mean per compatible 1 km² base cell, then clipped-water-area weighted mean of supported base cells; no missing-cell zero fill.
metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
metadata.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.

coastline.name: Natural Earth 1:10m land
coastline.limitations: Cartographic 1:10,000,000 coastline, not 10-metre spatial resolution. Small islands, tidal change and fine shorelines may be omitted; especially uncertain for 1 km² coastal cells. Natural Earth flags northern Russia and southern Chile coastline accuracy.

metadata.coastlineLimitations: Natural Earth 1:10 million cartographic land polygons; small islands, fine shorelines and tides may be missing. Coastal 1 km² cells are especially uncertain.
metadata.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

gradient.method: Gaussian-weighted visual interpolation within 75 km of a source point (25 km bandwidth). Not a validated pollution model or measured coverage.
gradient.waterMask: Natural Earth 1:10m with conservative raster edge buffer

colorScale.domainBasis: 0 to the 95th percentile of the selected source concentrations; colors saturate above this endpoint, displayed densities do not.
colorScale.note: Continuous concentration colors use a square-root scale; these are separate from the fixed SPI classification colors.

gradient.note: Continuous blue-to-red concentration scale. SPI classification remains available in tile details. Transparent beyond support or on land.
gradient.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

properties.source: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations

properties.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
properties.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.
properties.coverageMeaning: Fraction of tile water assigned a base-cell model estimate; not the fraction physically sampled.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

metadata.areaMethod: WGS84 ellipsoidal equal-area projected metres (EPSG:6933; polar caps EPSG:6931/6932)
metadata.aggregation: Latest-date mean per compatible 1 km² base cell, then clipped-water-area weighted mean of supported base cells; no missing-cell zero fill.
metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
metadata.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.

coastline.name: Natural Earth 1:10m land
coastline.limitations: Cartographic 1:10,000,000 coastline, not 10-metre spatial resolution. Small islands, tidal change and fine shorelines may be omitted; especially uncertain for 1 km² coastal cells. Natural Earth flags northern Russia and southern Chile coastline accuracy.

metadata.coastlineLimitations: Natural Earth 1:10 million cartographic land polygons; small islands, fine shorelines and tides may be missing. Coastal 1 km² cells are especially uncertain.
metadata.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

gradient.method: Gaussian-weighted visual interpolation within 75 km of a source point (25 km bandwidth). Not a validated pollution model or measured coverage.
gradient.waterMask: Natural Earth 1:10m with conservative raster edge buffer

colorScale.domainBasis: 0 to the 95th percentile of the selected source concentrations; colors saturate above this endpoint, displayed densities do not.
colorScale.note: Continuous concentration colors use a square-root scale; these are separate from the fixed SPI classification colors.

gradient.note: Continuous blue-to-red concentration scale. SPI classification remains available in tile details. Transparent beyond support or on land.
gradient.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

metadata.areaMethod: WGS84 ellipsoidal equal-area projected metres (EPSG:6933; polar caps EPSG:6931/6932)
metadata.aggregation: Latest-date mean per compatible 1 km² base cell, then clipped-water-area weighted mean of supported base cells; no missing-cell zero fill.
metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
metadata.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.

coastline.name: Natural Earth 1:10m land
coastline.limitations: Cartographic 1:10,000,000 coastline, not 10-metre spatial resolution. Small islands, tidal change and fine shorelines may be omitted; especially uncertain for 1 km² coastal cells. Natural Earth flags northern Russia and southern Chile coastline accuracy.

metadata.coastlineLimitations: Natural Earth 1:10 million cartographic land polygons; small islands, fine shorelines and tides may be missing. Coastal 1 km² cells are especially uncertain.
metadata.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

gradient.method: Gaussian-weighted visual interpolation within 75 km of a source point (25 km bandwidth). Not a validated pollution model or measured coverage.
gradient.waterMask: Natural Earth 1:10m with conservative raster edge buffer

colorScale.domainBasis: 0 to the 95th percentile of the selected source concentrations; colors saturate above this endpoint, displayed densities do not.
colorScale.note: Continuous concentration colors use a square-root scale; these are separate from the fixed SPI classification colors.

gradient.note: Continuous blue-to-red concentration scale. SPI classification remains available in tile details. Transparent beyond support or on land.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

metadata.areaMethod: WGS84 ellipsoidal equal-area projected metres (EPSG:6933; polar caps EPSG:6931/6932)
metadata.aggregation: Latest-date mean per compatible 1 km² base cell, then clipped-water-area weighted mean of supported base cells; no missing-cell zero fill.
metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
metadata.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.

coastline.name: Natural Earth 1:10m land
coastline.limitations: Cartographic 1:10,000,000 coastline, not 10-metre spatial resolution. Small islands, tidal change and fine shorelines may be omitted; especially uncertain for 1 km² coastal cells. Natural Earth flags northern Russia and southern Chile coastline accuracy.

metadata.coastlineLimitations: Natural Earth 1:10 million cartographic land polygons; small islands, fine shorelines and tides may be missing. Coastal 1 km² cells are especially uncertain.
metadata.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

gradient.method: Gaussian-weighted visual interpolation within 75 km of a source point (25 km bandwidth). Not a validated pollution model or measured coverage.
gradient.waterMask: Natural Earth 1:10m with conservative raster edge buffer

colorScale.domainBasis: 0 to the 95th percentile of the selected source concentrations; colors saturate above this endpoint, displayed densities do not.
colorScale.note: Continuous concentration colors use a square-root scale; these are separate from the fixed SPI classification colors.

gradient.note: Continuous blue-to-red concentration scale. SPI classification remains available in tile details. Transparent beyond support or on land.
gradient.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

metadata.areaMethod: WGS84 ellipsoidal equal-area projected metres (EPSG:6933; polar caps EPSG:6931/6932)
metadata.aggregation: Latest-date mean per compatible 1 km² base cell, then clipped-water-area weighted mean of supported base cells; no missing-cell zero fill.
metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
metadata.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.

coastline.name: Natural Earth 1:10m land
coastline.limitations: Cartographic 1:10,000,000 coastline, not 10-metre spatial resolution. Small islands, tidal change and fine shorelines may be omitted; especially uncertain for 1 km² coastal cells. Natural Earth flags northern Russia and southern Chile coastline accuracy.

metadata.coastlineLimitations: Natural Earth 1:10 million cartographic land polygons; small islands, fine shorelines and tides may be missing. Coastal 1 km² cells are especially uncertain.
metadata.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

gradient.method: Gaussian-weighted visual interpolation within 75 km of a source point (25 km bandwidth). Not a validated pollution model or measured coverage.
gradient.waterMask: Natural Earth 1:10m with conservative raster edge buffer

colorScale.domainBasis: 0 to the 95th percentile of the selected source concentrations; colors saturate above this endpoint, displayed densities do not.
colorScale.note: Continuous concentration colors use a square-root scale; these are separate from the fixed SPI classification colors.

gradient.note: Continuous blue-to-red concentration scale. SPI classification remains available in tile details. Transparent beyond support or on land.
gradient.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

metadata.areaMethod: WGS84 ellipsoidal equal-area projected metres (EPSG:6933; polar caps EPSG:6931/6932)
metadata.aggregation: Latest-date mean per compatible 1 km² base cell, then clipped-water-area weighted mean of supported base cells; no missing-cell zero fill.
metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
metadata.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.

coastline.name: Natural Earth 1:10m land
coastline.limitations: Cartographic 1:10,000,000 coastline, not 10-metre spatial resolution. Small islands, tidal change and fine shorelines may be omitted; especially uncertain for 1 km² coastal cells. Natural Earth flags northern Russia and southern Chile coastline accuracy.

metadata.coastlineLimitations: Natural Earth 1:10 million cartographic land polygons; small islands, fine shorelines and tides may be missing. Coastal 1 km² cells are especially uncertain.
metadata.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

gradient.method: Gaussian-weighted visual interpolation within 75 km of a source point (25 km bandwidth). Not a validated pollution model or measured coverage.
gradient.waterMask: Natural Earth 1:10m with conservative raster edge buffer

colorScale.domainBasis: 0 to the 95th percentile of the selected source concentrations; colors saturate above this endpoint, displayed densities do not.
colorScale.note: Continuous concentration colors use a square-root scale; these are separate from the fixed SPI classification colors.

gradient.note: Continuous blue-to-red concentration scale. SPI classification remains available in tile details. Transparent beyond support or on land.
gradient.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

metadata.areaMethod: WGS84 ellipsoidal equal-area projected metres (EPSG:6933; polar caps EPSG:6931/6932)
metadata.aggregation: Latest-date mean per compatible 1 km² base cell, then clipped-water-area weighted mean of supported base cells; no missing-cell zero fill.
metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
metadata.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.

coastline.name: Natural Earth 1:10m land
coastline.limitations: Cartographic 1:10,000,000 coastline, not 10-metre spatial resolution. Small islands, tidal change and fine shorelines may be omitted; especially uncertain for 1 km² coastal cells. Natural Earth flags northern Russia and southern Chile coastline accuracy.

metadata.coastlineLimitations: Natural Earth 1:10 million cartographic land polygons; small islands, fine shorelines and tides may be missing. Coastal 1 km² cells are especially uncertain.
metadata.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

gradient.method: Gaussian-weighted visual interpolation within 75 km of a source point (25 km bandwidth). Not a validated pollution model or measured coverage.
gradient.waterMask: Natural Earth 1:10m with conservative raster edge buffer

colorScale.domainBasis: 0 to the 95th percentile of the selected source concentrations; colors saturate above this endpoint, displayed densities do not.
colorScale.note: Continuous concentration colors use a square-root scale; these are separate from the fixed SPI classification colors.

gradient.note: Continuous blue-to-red concentration scale. SPI classification remains available in tile details. Transparent beyond support or on land.
gradient.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

metadata.areaMethod: WGS84 ellipsoidal equal-area projected metres (EPSG:6933; polar caps EPSG:6931/6932)
metadata.aggregation: Latest-date mean per compatible 1 km² base cell, then clipped-water-area weighted mean of supported base cells; no missing-cell zero fill.
metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
metadata.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.

coastline.name: Natural Earth 1:10m land
coastline.limitations: Cartographic 1:10,000,000 coastline, not 10-metre spatial resolution. Small islands, tidal change and fine shorelines may be omitted; especially uncertain for 1 km² coastal cells. Natural Earth flags northern Russia and southern Chile coastline accuracy.

metadata.coastlineLimitations: Natural Earth 1:10 million cartographic land polygons; small islands, fine shorelines and tides may be missing. Coastal 1 km² cells are especially uncertain.
metadata.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

gradient.method: Gaussian-weighted visual interpolation within 75 km of a source point (25 km bandwidth). Not a validated pollution model or measured coverage.
gradient.waterMask: Natural Earth 1:10m with conservative raster edge buffer

colorScale.domainBasis: 0 to the 95th percentile of the selected source concentrations; colors saturate above this endpoint, displayed densities do not.
colorScale.note: Continuous concentration colors use a square-root scale; these are separate from the fixed SPI classification colors.

gradient.note: Continuous blue-to-red concentration scale. SPI classification remains available in tile details. Transparent beyond support or on land.
gradient.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

coverage.selection: All compatible marine point records returned by the provider; no downsampling or spatial interpolation

source.snapshotNote: Precomputed snapshot exported from published historical observations; not a live feed or complete pollution coverage. Tile geometry represents supported base-cell water. Smooth colors are bounded visual interpolation, not measured coverage.

metadata.aggregation: Latest-date mean per compatible 1 km² base cell, then clipped-water-area weighted mean of supported base cells; no missing-cell zero fill.
metadata.supportMethod: Selected latest point observations averaged inside a fixed 1 km² equal-area base cell; cell water is a model estimate, not surveyed coverage.
metadata.selectionMethod: Latest UTC calendar date per fixed 1 km² base cell and material scope; average ties on that date. Use undated observations only when that base cell has no dated observations.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.

The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.

source.name: Oceaneye surface micro- and mesoplastic point observations
source.unitConversion: None; particles and pieces both denote the source particle count
limitations: Historical net-tow locations, not a live pollution feed or complete global coverage; unsampled water is unknown.
The units describe source-reported surface micro- and mesoplastic particles, not all-size debris, mass, toxicity, or satellite-detected objects.
Tows sample approximately the upper 0.15 m with 0.33 mm mesh; values are already reported in particles/km2 and are copied without volumetric conversion.

From 2015 onward the published method estimates the 0.33-1 mm fraction from larger measured particles. These are conservatively labeled model (model-assisted net-tow observations), inferred from sample year because the export has no per-row model flag.
No per-observation uncertainty is supplied by this point export. Null uncertainty means unavailable, not zero; no confidence or error bound is invented.
The model-method report gives 28% average relative error for numerical concentration on its evaluation set; that is not a per-observation uncertainty or confidence interval.
Provider region labels exclude lakes and rivers. Irregular volunteer sampling, particle identification, wind mixing, and method differences limit comparisons and extrapolation.
The live map group is updated through 2025, while its capabilities abstract and project identifier retain older dates. Observation dates come from each source record.
